title: SLO dependency graph and error-budget reallocation procedure
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Problem: When a region/model suffers a sustained quality or latency degradation, current heuristics for load-shedding and fallback operate independently per-endpoint and lack a canonical representation of upstream/downstream dependencies. This causes suboptimal error-budget charging, double-counting across related routes, and ad-hoc priority decisions. Goal: Deliver a specification and prototype implementation for a SLO dependency graph plus a deterministic error-budget reallocation procedure (aka burn reallocation) that: 1) models relationships between routes, model variants, and regional capacity 2) computes per-node effective burn rates and credit pools, 3) provides a ranked reallocation plan for preserving high-value routes and minimizing customer-visible regressions, and 4) exposes telemetry + audits to justify automated or manual interventions.
acceptance_criteria: Spec doc describing graph model, node types (route, variant, region, capacity-pool), and edge semantics (flows, credit-transfer rules)
Algorithm pseudocode for computing effective burn and candidate reallocation actions given a set of degraded nodes
Prototype service that computes reallocation recommendations from simulated incidents (unit tests + deterministic outputs)

Integration test verifying reallocation recommendation applied to a synthetic multi-region traffic snapshot preserves >=90% of high-priority route availability while reducing aggregate burn on degraded region by >=40%
Dashboard panels showing per-node credit pools and reallocation history; audit log retained for 90 days
Operational runbook for triggering automated reallocation vs manual approval with clear SLO gates and circuit-breaker thresholds

implementation_notes: Graph model will be stored as adjacency list in our existing graph-store (extend current SLO metadata index)
Compute layer runs as a batch job every 15s in the control-plane; prototype will be synchronous for deterministic tests
Credit pools are represented as floating point 'credits' proportional to remaining error budget in the evaluation window
Reallocation actions are recommendations (defer actuator implementation to follow-up ticket); actions include partial throttles, variant demotion, and regional diversion
Backpressure semantics: when an upstream node is rate-limited, we mark downstream impact and propagate softened allocations rather than hard cuts to avoid cascading failures
design_decisions: Use directed edges to represent consumption direction (route -> variant -> region). This simplifies burn attribution calculations
Keep reallocation deterministic (no randomized tie-breakers). Determinism eases testability and forensics
Do not auto-enact reallocation for high-risk customer-impact incidents. Start with recommended mode and an opt-in automated path protected by strict SLO gates
Represent credits on a normalized 0..1 scale per SLO window and allow weighted transfers based on route priority scores
tradeoffs: Complexity vs transparency: Graph model increases metadata surface area but provides clear attribution; initial storage cost is higher
Frequency vs stability: 15s compute cadence gives responsiveness but risks oscillation; will add hysteresis in policy layer
Automated vs manual control: Manual-first reduces blast radius but increases MTTR; plan staged automation with strict canarying
monitoring_and_alerting: Alert: graph compute failure -> P1; alert: reallocation recommendation rejects -> P2
Dashboards: per-node remaining credit, burn rate heatmap, reallocation suggestion queue, incidents where recommendations were applied
Audit: store every computed recommendation with input snapshot and deterministic hash for later replay and postmortem
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (spec + prototype): internal review, unit tests, synthetic integration tests (target: runtime-1.22-canary)
Phase 2 (read-only telemetry + dashboard): enable graph ingestion in staging and surface recommendations in Console without actuation
Phase 3 (controlled automation): enable actuator for low-risk routes behind a feature flag and run controlled DR scenarios
Phase 4 (broader rollout): open automation for additional routes after 2 successful DRs and SRE sign-off
test_plan: Unit tests for graph construction and burn calculation with edge cases: cycles, disconnected nodes, and overlapping SLO windows
Deterministic integration tests using recorded traffic traces from past incidents (redacted) to validate recommendations match expected policy
Chaos test: simulate flapping region capacity and verify hysteresis prevents oscillation
Manual DR exercise in staging: validate console workflow, audit logs, and rollback behavior
